# Gateway vs. HTTP Interactions

Covers how Discord bots connect and communicate: WebSocket gateway, REST API,
and HTTP interaction endpoints. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full
source details.

## Connection Architecture

Discord bots use two primary communication channels: a persistent **WebSocket
gateway** for receiving real-time events, and the **REST API** for performing
actions. These are complementary — most bots use both. [1]

A third option, the **HTTP interactions endpoint**, replaces the gateway for
bots that only handle slash commands and other interactions. [2] [3]

## Gateway (WebSocket)

| Property | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| URL format | `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json` | [1] |
| Encoding options | JSON, ETF (binary) | [1] |
| Compression | zlib-stream, zstd-stream (optional) | [1] |
| URL discovery | `GET /gateway/bot` (authed, includes shard info) | [1] |
| Heartbeat | Interval from Hello event; jitter on first beat | [1] |
| Max payload | 4096 bytes (close code 4002 if exceeded) | [1] |
| Event rate limit | 120 events per 60 seconds per connection | [1] |
| Identify limit | 1000 per 24 hours (global, all shards) | [1] |

### Connection Lifecycle

1. Connect to gateway URL via WebSocket [1]
2. Receive Hello (opcode 10) with `heartbeat_interval` [1]
3. Send first heartbeat after `heartbeat_interval * random(0,1)` [1]
4. Send Identify (opcode 2) with token, intents, properties [1]
5. Receive Ready with `session_id` and `resume_gateway_url` [1]
6. Maintain heartbeat; receive Heartbeat ACK (opcode 11) [1]
7. Missing ACK = "zombied connection" — terminate and reconnect [1]

### Opcodes

| Opcode | Name | Direction | Purpose |
|--------|------|-----------|---------|
| 0 | Dispatch | Server → Client | Event data (MESSAGE_CREATE, etc.) |
| 1 | Heartbeat | Bidirectional | Keep-alive ping |
| 2 | Identify | Client → Server | Authentication handshake |
| 3 | Update Presence | Client → Server | Set status/activity |
| 6 | Resume | Client → Server | Reconnect to existing session |
| 7 | Reconnect | Server → Client | Server requests reconnection |
| 9 | Invalid Session | Server → Client | Auth failed (d: true/false) |
| 10 | Hello | Server → Client | heartbeat_interval provided |
| 11 | Heartbeat ACK | Server → Client | Acknowledge heartbeat |

[1]

### Resume Protocol

Resume (opcode 6) reconnects without re-identifying, using `resume_gateway_url`
from Ready, the cached `session_id`, and last sequence number. Triggers include:
Reconnect event (opcode 7), resumable close codes, disconnect without close code,
or Invalid Session with `d: true`. [1]

Failure (Invalid Session with `d: false`) requires a full re-identify. [1]

### Close Codes

| Code | Name | Resumable |
|------|------|-----------|
| 4007 | Invalid Seq | Yes |
| 4009 | Session Timeout | Yes |
| 1000, 1001 | Normal/Going Away | No |
| 4002-4005 | Decode/Auth errors | No |
| 4008 | Rate Limited | No |
| 4010-4014 | Shard/Intent errors | No |

[1]

## HTTP Interactions Endpoint

An alternative to the gateway for receiving **interaction events only** (slash
commands, buttons, modals, context menus). [2] [3]

| Property | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| Delivery | Discord POSTs to your configured URL | [2] |
| Security | Ed25519 signatures via X-Signature-Ed25519 and X-Signature-Timestamp | [3] |
| Validation | Invalid signatures must return 401 | [3] |
| Verification | Respond to PING (type 1) with PONG (type 1) | [2] |
| Response deadline | 3 seconds for initial response | [2] |
| Token validity | 15 minutes for followup operations | [2] |

The two delivery methods are **mutually exclusive** — "An app cannot use both
simultaneously." [2]

### What HTTP Endpoint Cannot Do

The HTTP endpoint only receives interaction payloads. It cannot receive:
- Message events (MESSAGE_CREATE, MESSAGE_UPDATE, etc.)
- Member join/leave events
- Presence updates
- Any other gateway-only events [2]

## REST API

The REST API is used for performing actions: sending messages, managing roles,
updating channels. Both gateway-based and HTTP-interaction-based bots use the
REST API for outbound operations. Rate limits apply (see
[rate-limits-constraints.md](rate-limits-constraints.md)). [4]

## Architectural Choice for Personal Automation

| Factor | Gateway | HTTP Endpoint |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| Can read messages | Yes (with intents) | No |
| Can receive reactions | Yes | No |
| Requires persistent process | Yes | No (serverless-friendly) |
| Interaction support | Yes | Yes |
| Presence/status display | Yes | No |
| Complexity | Higher (WebSocket, heartbeat, resume) | Lower (HTTP POST handler) |

A personal automation bot that needs **bidirectional communication** (reading
messages, reacting to events, displaying presence) must use the gateway. A bot
that only responds to slash commands could use the HTTP endpoint. [1] [2] [3]

## Gaps and Limitations

- REST API per-route rate limits are not enumerated in documentation; they are
  communicated only via response headers [4]
- The exact behavior when switching between gateway and HTTP endpoint modes
  (e.g., reconfiguration latency) is not documented
